solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rebel's to confirm getting framed in Dundee, perhaps

indicators.note: a picture framed in something sits inside it, so the confirming word goes inside the name

parts.note: Mick Dundee is the hero of the film Crocodile Dundee, so Dundee is one example of a Mick
to aver is to state firmly or confirm

explanation.surface: A rebel being pictured, framed, in the Scottish city of Dundee.
explanation.walkthrough: Dundee looks like the Scottish city, but it is Mick 'Crocodile' Dundee of the 1980s film. The 's is 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a maverick is an independent-minded person who refuses to follow the herd.

clue.text: Middle-of-the-road journalist with Independent punches bloke

indicators.note: to punch is to make a hole, so the pieces go into the bloke

parts.note: a bloke is a man
ED, editor, is the crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A moderate journalist on the Independent newspaper punching a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'punches' drives ED and I into MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The median is the middle value, so it is middle-of-the-road.

clue.text: Seller travelled around north, rising after five

indicators.note: after puts the reversed piece behind the numeral

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means read upwards, so the piece is reversed
the travelled word goes around the letter for north

parts.note: rode means travelled
N is north

explanation.surface: A seller travelling round the north, getting up after five.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts N in RODE, giving RONDE, which 'rising' turns into ENDOR, placed after V.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a vendor is someone who sells, a trader.

clue.text: Corrupt men that will make revolutions

parts.note: to rot is to decay or corrupt
OR, other ranks, are enlisted men in the army

explanation.surface: Corrupt men plotting a political revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: Revolutions looks political but means turns of a wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, such as helicopter blades, which spins round.

clue.text: Axe Commonwealth's top jumper

indicators.note: in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a hopper is something that jumps, like a grasshopper

explanation.surface: The best jumper in the Commonwealth being dropped.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumper looks like a British sweater or an athlete, but is a hopper.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a chopper is an axe or cleaver.

clue.text: Liveliness displayed by imp cycling backwards

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for an imp cycles round to the front, travelling backwards

parts.note: a sprite is a small mischievous fairy, an imp

explanation.surface: A lively little imp riding a bicycle in reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling backwards' moves the final E of SPRITE to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: esprit is French-derived for spirit, wit and vivacity.

clue.text: Queen in Dickens novel laughed

indicators.note: the queen goes in, inside, the reworked name
novel means new, so the letters are given a fresh order

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A queen in a Dickens novel laughing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but is the anagram signal: DICKENS rearranged, with ER in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to snicker is to laugh in a half-suppressed, sly way.

clue.text: Limit supply going to empty arsenal — that's intelligent

parts.note: to ration is to limit the supply of something

indicators.note: an emptied word keeps only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Restricting the supply of weapons to an empty arsenal is a sensible move.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal could be the London football club, but it is just the word emptied to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: rational means able to reason, sensible and intelligent.

clue.text: Steal from sales

definitions.meaning: in basketball and other ball games, winning the ball from an opponent
the total amount of business a firm does

explanation.surface: Stealing goods from a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: In basketball a steal results in a turnover, losing possession; turnover is also a firm's revenue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: losing the ball to opponents, and the gross sales revenue of a business.

clue.text: Perform state offering

parts.note: to do a play is to perform it
a nation is a state or country

explanation.surface: A state ceremony or performance at which a gift is offered.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a donation is a gift offered, typically to a charity.

clue.text: Season drink containing drop of tequila and drop of rum

indicators.note: the drink holds the first letter of tequila inside it

parts.note: wine is a drink

indicators.note: a drop of something is a tiny bit, here its first letter
again a drop is just the opening letter, this time of rum

explanation.surface: Seasoning a drink with a splash of tequila and rum, a winter cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' puts T inside WINE; the R from rum goes on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: winter is one of the four seasons of the year.

clue.text: Trade centre vehicle that's on the up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A trade centre selling vehicles, business on the rise.
explanation.definitionFit: A mart is a market or trading centre.

clue.text: Approach nervously about unknown books of uncertain origin

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, surrounding, the unknown
doing something nervously makes it jittery and disordered, so the letters are shuffled

parts.note: in algebra x, y and z are unknowns; here Y

explanation.surface: Someone timidly approaching some mysterious old books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervously' rearranges APPROACH into APOCRPHA, and 'about' wraps that around Y.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocrypha are biblical or other writings whose authorship or authenticity is doubtful.

clue.text: Enemy finally took out former capital

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged
finally points to the last letter of enemy

explanation.surface: The enemy eventually wiped out an old capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' shuffles TOOK with the Y from 'Enemy finally' to give KYOTO.
explanation.definitionFit: Kyoto was the imperial seat of Japan for over a thousand years before Tokyo took over.

clue.text: Back in arrears

indicators.note: the answer lies in, inside, the word arrears

explanation.surface: Being behind with payments, in arrears.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: the rear is the back of something.

clue.text: Finish wretched run with ace stamina

parts.note: the end is the finish

indicators.note: wretched suggests something wrecked and messed up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner completing a miserable run, needing ace stamina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wretched' rearranges RUN with ACE into URANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: endurance is the capacity to keep going, stamina.

clue.text: Half come back from the east and rush platform

indicators.note: in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left, backwards
half of the six-letter synonym, its first three letters

parts.note: to return is to come back
to race is to rush

explanation.surface: Coming back from the east and rushing to a station platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half' keeps RET from RETURN and 'from the east' turns it to TER.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrace is a raised level platform, as on a hillside or beside a house.

clue.text: Rocky islands in Shetlands and Tuscany, where one's returned

parts.note: Unst is the most northerly of the Shetland Islands

indicators.note: of the two islands, one is turned back, read in reverse

parts.note: Elba is an island off Tuscany

explanation.surface: Rocky islands off Shetland and Tuscany, where someone has come back.
explanation.walkthrough: Elba is where Napoleon was exiled; reversed it gives ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocky here means shaky or wobbly, not stable.

clue.text: Hard to leave hermitage when unsettled — one needs to resettle?

indicators.note: unsettled means disturbed, so the remaining letters are jumbled
leave means go away, so the letter is removed

parts.note: H is hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone forced out of a hermitage needing to resettle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to leave' takes H out of HERMITAGE, and 'when unsettled' shuffles ERMITAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To emigrate is to leave one's country to make a new home elsewhere.

clue.text: Moan about cops retiring unsettled

indicators.note: about here means turned around and rearranged, signalling a shuffle
retiring means drawing back, so the word for cops is reversed

parts.note: the CID, Criminal Investigation Department, is the UK detective branch of the police

explanation.surface: Someone grumbling that the police are withdrawing, leaving things unsettled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges MOAN as NOMA; 'retiring' turns CID into DIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomadic people have no settled home, moving from place to place.

clue.text: Talk about Derby?

parts.note: C, circa, means about
a derby is a bowler hat

explanation.surface: Discussion about the Derby horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is a famous English horse race, but here a derby is a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to chat is to talk informally.

clue.text: Green exhaust

definitions.meaning: a green colour like that of the precious stone
to tire out or wear down

explanation.surface: Green car exhaust, an environmental picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Jade is a green gemstone and its colour; to jade is to tire or weary.

clue.text: Stimulating exercise

definitions.meaning: prompting, as in nudging someone's memory
running at a slow, steady pace for fitness

explanation.surface: A double definition with no picture beyond stimulating exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Jogging a memory stimulates it; jogging is also running steadily as exercise.

clue.text: Prestige and pain in court

indicators.note: the pain goes in, inside, the court abbreviation

parts.note: an ache is a pain

explanation.surface: Prestige and pain in a court of law.
explanation.definitionFit: Cachet is distinction or prestige.

clue.text: Presume trick involves system of weights and measures

indicators.note: the phrase involves, contains, the answer within it

explanation.surface: Assuming a trick is involved in the weights and measures system.
explanation.definitionFit: The metric system is the decimal system of measurement based on metres and kilograms.

clue.text: Row about good and formidable opponent

indicators.note: the row goes about, surrounding, the letter for good

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: An argument about something good with a formidable rival.
explanation.walkthrough: Row looks like a quarrel but is a tier of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: a tiger is a fierce, aggressive competitor.

clue.text: Annoy crooked garage claiming tax

indicators.note: claiming means taking in, so the shuffled letters hold the tax
crooked means bent out of shape, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: VAT is value added tax

explanation.surface: A dishonest garage charging tax and annoying the customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' gives AGGRAE and 'claiming' takes the tax inside; VAT is the UK's value added tax on sales.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in informal use: to aggravate someone is to irritate them.

clue.text: Friend's run after another

indicators.note: the run comes after the other word

parts.note: ami, French for friend, is another word for friend
to go is to run

explanation.surface: A friend going for a run after another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another friend: AMI in French. The 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is Spanish for friend, also used in English.

clue.text: Support one city? Clever!

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
I is the Roman numeral one
NY is New York city

explanation.surface: Backing a single city is a clever move.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a brainy person is intelligent.

clue.text: In international, overwhelmed by playing fresh striker

indicators.note: overwhelmed means engulfed, so the pieces sit inside the shuffled letters
playing here means acting up or moving about, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A footballer winning an international cap, overshadowed by a fresh striker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' and 'overwhelmed by' work together: the shuffle of the last word wraps the international pieces. Striker is a football forward, not someone hitting out.
explanation.definitionFit: In football, a finisher is a striker who reliably converts chances into goals.

clue.text: Thus the chancellor begins his address in the Spanish uniform

definitions.text: Thus the chancellor begins his address

parts.note: el is the Spanish definite article
even means uniform or level

explanation.surface: A chancellor opening a speech in a Spanish uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: The UK Chancellor of the Exchequer lives at 11 Downing Street, so his address starts with that number.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic hint: the Chancellor's official London residence is number 11 Downing Street.

clue.text: Sit around during dance backing non-believer

indicators.note: during means within, so the shuffled letters go inside the dance
backing means going backwards, so the dance's name is reversed

parts.note: a conga is a dance performed in a line

indicators.note: around signals the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Sitting out a dance while others go backwards: an unbeliever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' gives AGNOC; 'around' shuffles the sitting letters and 'during' puts them inside. The conga is a party line dance.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic holds that the existence of God is unknowable, so is not a believer.
